title: New Jersey Home Battery Rebates 2026: PSE&G GridSmart Up to $5,000
desc: New Jersey home battery rebates in 2026: PSE&G pays up to $5,000 through GridSmart, JCP&L and Atlantic City Electric have none we found, and the federal credit ended.
h1: New Jersey Home Battery Rebates in 2026
lead: A home battery keeps lights, a refrigerator and a few other things running when the power goes out. In New Jersey, one utility pays for it: PSE&G, through a program called GridSmart. Other customers have no utility battery rebate that we could find, and the federal credit ended. Here is how GridSmart works, what it asks of you, and what the state is planning.
cards_heading: Battery money in New Jersey in 2026
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page.

cards.title: PSE&G GridSmart Battery Program
cards.note: An instant rebate on the contractor's invoice, plus up to $25,000 of interest-free repayment on your bill. For PSE&G electric or dual-fuel customers. New installs only.

cards.title: Garden State Energy Storage Program
cards.note: The state released a plan for about 150 megawatts of storage that includes options for home batteries. It has no amounts or start date yet.

cards.title: Federal 25D battery credit
cards.note: The 30% credit does not apply to batteries paid for after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: JCP&L and Atlantic City Electric are not on the list. On the pages we read, neither utility offers a home battery rebate. Check your electric bill, because the answer depends on the name printed there.
sections: The rebate is not free money. In return, you agree to let PSE&G run your battery during up to 100 events a year, each up to four hours, when demand on the grid is high. PSE&G sends an email before each event. If the battery falls to 20% charge, your house goes back to the grid so you keep a reserve. PSE&G says it will not call an event during an outage. You also agree to share data from the battery.

PSE&G lists three approved batteries: Tesla Powerwall 3, Enphase 10C and Enphase 5P. At least two Enphase 5P units are needed to reach the minimum size of 8.5 kilowatts of storage. You need a smart meter and a Wi-Fi connection. Leased batteries and batteries already in place do not qualify, and the program has a cap on total participants. The state is looking at ways to let existing batteries join later.

PSE&G says plainly that the program is meant to give you backup power, and that it will not inherently save you money on bills. Customers on PSE&G's time-of-use rate may save more by charging off-peak and using the battery at peak times. Think of the rebate as lowering the price of insurance against outages, not as a way to earn a return.
How long can it run the house?

PSE&G says modern batteries can power the needs of most homes for about 11 hours, depending on size and use. That is the company's figure, not a promise for your home. Ask your contractor to list the circuits the battery will run and for how long, in writing.

You can install a battery with or without solar panels. Solar hardware is not covered by the battery rebate or repayment. If you add panels, the state's solar credits and net metering apply separately. Read our solar guide to see how those work.
claim_heading: How to get the PSE&G battery rebate
claim_steps: Check that your bill says PSE&G and that you have a smart meter and Wi-Fi.
Pick a participating GridSmart contractor from PSE&G's list. You must use one.
Choose one of the three approved batteries and size it for the circuits you want to run.
Let the contractor apply for you. The rebate comes off the invoice.
Pass the final inspection so your battery can join the program.

faq: Is there a home battery rebate in New Jersey?
Yes, for PSE&G customers: up to $5,000 through GridSmart. We found none from JCP&L or Atlantic City Electric.
Can I use a Tesla Powerwall?
Yes. Powerwall 3 is on PSE&G's approved list, along with Enphase 10C and 5P.
Can I add a battery to a system I already have?
Only new installations qualify at this time. A battery that is already installed does not.
Is the federal battery credit open?
No. It ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
Will the state add a battery program?
The state has released a proposal with options for home batteries, but it has no amounts or start date yet.
